lyrics:
[Intro: fast hammered single-string guitar riff alone, hi-hat ticking]

[Chant: low gang voices over the riff, kick drum joins]
(Whoa-oh, oh-oh) Voltage!
(Whoa-oh, oh-oh) Voltage!
(Whoa-oh, oh-oh) Voltage!
(Whoa-oh, oh-oh) Voltage!

[Verse 1: rasping high vocal, rhythm guitar and full drums crash in]
I was parked out in the driveway with the engine cold
Somebody on the radio said I was getting old
Felt it in my knuckles, felt it in my knees
Then a spark came crawling up the back of me

[Pre-Chorus: stabs, snare builds]
And the garage door shook
And the neighbours came to look

[Chorus: open ringing chords, gang answers]
I still got the voltage (yeah, yeah, yeah)
Still got the voltage (yeah, yeah, yeah)
Ran a line down from the sky into my bones
I still got the voltage

[Verse 2: rasping high vocal over the riff]
Dug my boots out from the bottom of the stairs
Found a jacket that remembers when I didn't care
My kid said "who are you?" and I said "wait and see"
Kicked the amp awake and it remembered me

[Pre-Chorus: stabs, snare builds]
And the windows shook
And the whole street came to look

[Chorus: open ringing chords, gang answers]
I still got the voltage (yeah, yeah, yeah)
Still got the voltage (yeah, yeah, yeah)
Ran a line down from the sky into my bones
I still got the voltage

[Guitar Solo: blues-rock, fast runs, wide vibrato]

[Bridge: drums and chant only, call and response]
Plug it in (plug it in)
Turn it up (turn it up)
Plug it in (plug it in)
Burn it up (burn it up)

[Final Chorus: full band, lead guitar wailing over the top]
I still got the voltage (yeah, yeah, yeah)
Still got the voltage (yeah, yeah, yeah)
Ran a line down from the sky into my bones
I still got the voltage
Still got the voltage

[Outro: hammered riff returns, chant, final crash]
(Whoa-oh, oh-oh) Voltage!
(Whoa-oh, oh-oh) Voltage!
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 134 BPM, 4/4, in B with a blues-rock flavour. Relentless, driving, built for a crowd.

VOICE: Male, very high and rasping, a controlled shriek that sits above the guitars. Verses are rhythmic and clipped. A gang of low male voices chants the wordless line and shouts the title word and the answers.

INSTRUMENTS: Lead electric guitar playing a rapid, even figure of hammered notes on one string, clean but biting. Second electric guitar with a crunchy, open-chord rhythm sound. Thick, simple bass on root notes. A dry, enormous drum kit: hi-hat first, then kick, then the full kit. No keyboards.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the hammered riff alone with a ticking hi-hat. 0:14 The chant enters with a kick drum on every beat. 0:43 Rhythm guitar, bass and full drums crash in for verse 1. 1:11 Pre-chorus. 1:20 Chorus 1. 1:41 Verse 2. 2:09 Pre-chorus. 2:18 Chorus 2. 2:39 Guitar solo over the verse riff. 3:07 Bridge, everything drops to drums and call-and-response shouting. 3:25 Final chorus, with the lead guitar soloing over it. 3:53 Outro, the riff and the chant, last crash at 4:10.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Dry, loud, wide and uncluttered. Two guitars panned apart, drums natural and huge, very little reverb.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first shout of the title word at 0:14, when the kick drum joins the riff.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The tall tale is now about a middle-aged man in a driveway. The boast is not that he is young, it is that the current still runs. A sub layer under the kick gives it modern weight.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Doubt for two lines, then pure swagger.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

A man who has been told he is past it sits in his driveway, feels a spark climb his spine, and goes to find his boots.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a mid-life comeback; an athlete returning from injury; an old band reforming; a heart restarted in an ambulance; or a pre-game chant that needs no story at all.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: a fast hammered guitar figure that starts alone, a one-word chant, drums that enter in stages, and a tall tale told as a boast. Designed mishearing: 'still got the voltage' is heard as 'still got the old age', which is the joke the song is answering.
